prediction_question: Given everything documented about a mine and its own prior inspections and citations before an inspection begins, which of the declared set of 30 CFR sections will MSHA cite at this inspection?
prediction_time: The instant the inspection begins (INSPECTION_BEGIN_DT). Every feature is either a static mine attribute (Mines table), the inspection's own trigger recorded when it opens (ACTIVITY_CODE/ACTIVITY, PROGRAM_AREA, INSPECT_OFFICE_CD), or a field of an earlier inspection of the same MINE_ID. Everything the inspector observes or records during the visit is post-hoc and excluded.
target_definition: The set of 30 CFR sections cited at one inspection (EVENT_NO), i.e. the distinct PART_SECTION values of its violation rows - multi-label, mean 5.79 sections per inspection, median 2. The raw label space is 5,934 sections; construction declares a floor (104 sections at >= 1% of inspections, 183 at >= 0.5%). PART_SECTION itself and every violation-level attribute of the cited rows are excluded from the shipped features.

license_evidence.field: Terms on the MSHA data-set landing page and the Violations definition file
license_evidence.quote: The MSHA data-sources pages publish the files, the column definitions and update frequency; they state no licence, no terms of use and no redistribution permission.
license_evidence.terms: Silent on redistribution - contract #1 is therefore unresolved.

license_evidence.field: data.gov catalogue entry for the MSHA Violations Dataset
license_evidence.quote: accessLevel: public; rights: "true"; publisher: Mine Safety and Health Administration; temporal 2000-01-01 to present. The entry names no licence.
license_evidence.terms: public-domain status is by statute (US federal government work), not by a quotable licence.

license_evidence.field: Third-party precedent for treating MSHA federal works as redistributable (precedent, not permission)
license_evidence.quote: emperor-mew/msha-violations declares license: cc0-1.0 for its derived MSHA data and states the underlying federal works are US public domain (it cites 17 USC 105 and '5 USC 105'); FastDOLz/msha-mine-safety-violations-by-operator publishes a CC-BY-4.0 mirror of the same source and registers it on Zenodo.
license_evidence.terms: Two independent third parties already redistribute derived MSHA data under an open dedication. This supports the statutory reading but is not a licence grant from the publisher, so the escalation in license_decision stands.

license_decision: UNRESOLVED - escalate to the operator before construction. The source states no terms; the only basis for redistribution is that this is a work of the US federal government, which is a statutory argument, not a licence we can quote. Two options to decide between: (a) treat US federal works as public domain, record that reasoning and the data.gov accessLevel=public entry, and proceed; or (b) require an explicit written permission/source before construction. Do not assume (a) silently - contract #1 says a source silent on redistribution is escalated, never assumed.
split_strategy: Temporal by inspection year, no random component, three disjoint windows: train 2001-2020 (415,088 inspections / 2,459,741 citations), eval 2021-2023 (49,233 / 255,952), holdout 2024-2025 (33,576 / 175,151). Every one of the 104 sections at the >= 1% floor occurs in every window (checked by probe_splits.py). 2000 (19,640 inspections) is the earliest full year and folds into train; 2026 is partial and is not used.

measurements.measured_by: anonymous download and streamed probes (probe_violations.py, probe_splits.py); no credentials, nothing extracted to disk

the inspection's own trigger, recorded when it opens: ACTIVITY_CODE/ACTIVITY, PROGRAM_AREA, INSPECT_OFFICE_CD

post_hoc_never_shipped: SIG_SUB, NEGLIGENCE, LIKELIHOOD, INJ_ILLNESS, NO_AFFECTED, ENFORCEMENT_AREA, SPECIAL_ASSESS
SECTION_OF_ACT, SECTION_OF_ACT_1, SECTION_OF_ACT_2, CIT_ORD_SAFE, VIOLATION_NO, PART_SECTION
every date after the begin date: VIOLATION_ISSUE_DT, ORIG_TERM_DUE_DT, LATEST_TERM_DUE_DT, TERMINATION_DT, VACATE_DT, FINAL_ORDER_ISSUE_DT
PROPOSED_PENALTY, AMOUNT_DUE, AMOUNT_PAID, docket and contest fields
end-of-visit inspection counts: TOTAL_ON_SITE_HOURS, TOTAL_INSP_HOURS, SAMPLE_CNT_*, area-with-Y flags
feature_plan.decide_at_construction: NBR_INSPECTORS and ACTIVE_SECTIONS - whether they are known when the inspection opens or only as it proceeds; default exclude.

next_action: LICENCE DECISION NEEDED (one operator decision) - then construction on a worker. (1) Decide contract #1: the source states no terms; choose between treating US federal works as public domain with the data.gov accessLevel=public entry recorded, or requiring explicit permission. (2) On approval, budget a worker construction pass (the 120 MB weekly zip + Mines/Inspections companion tables), run skills/dataset-qualification, and only then quote any number. (3) Decide the label floor (104 at >= 1% or 183 at >= 0.5%), the treatment of mine-wide audit events (tail to 694 citations), and whether coal and metal/non-metal ship as two configs. Nothing is constructed. This candidate supersedes chicago-food-inspections as the multi-label lead.

novelty_check.theirs: MSHA ships the raw tables, the definition files, MDRS and descriptive calculators (S&S rate, pattern of violations), but no prediction task and no splits. Mine-safety ML prior art predicts accidents/injuries or violation counts, or which mines to inspect (binary targeting): Univ. of Kentucky thesis 'Temporal Machine Learning for Predicting Accidents and Violations at Surface Coal Mines', 'Machine Learning Classification Models for More Effective Mine Safety Inspections', Marshall's random-forest pattern study, and the ASCE-ASME J. Risk enforcement-action study. OSHA-side work is establishment targeting, not a cited-standard set. Two Hugging Face artifacts that mention MSHA were opened and read on 2026-09-27 and neither is this task: emperor-mew/msha-violations is a dataset card with no data files (it points at a live REST API for citation-level records), and FastDOLz/msha-mine-safety-violations-by-operator is operator-level aggregation (40,720 operators, 3,076,282 violations rolled up with penalty totals and cross-agency OSHA/WHD indicators, CC-BY-4.0, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20572372). No package ships the inspection-level multi-label set of cited sections with a prediction instant and splits.
novelty_check.ours: The multi-label formulation itself: one row per MSHA inspection, target = the set of 30 CFR sections cited at that inspection (104 sections at a >=1% floor, 183 at >=0.5%), with an explicit prediction instant at INSPECTION_BEGIN_DT, a pre-inspection-only feature set drawn from the Mines table plus the mine's own inspection and citation history, and three disjoint temporal windows (2001-2020 / 2021-2023 / 2024-2025) each holding every floor label. No ML-ready package ships this task.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
